findings.claim: revisionist historians led by A.J.P. Taylor and later R.A.C. Parker ... Parker acknowledged British public opinion was strongly against another war ... and that Chamberlain's options were more limited than his critics allowed.
findings.truth: Parker argued the opposite. In 'Chamberlain and Appeasement' he rejected the 'buying time' defence and argued Chamberlain had real alternatives, including a Soviet alliance, and refused them. Lesson 12 of this same unit states Parker's argument correctly, so the unit contradicted itself. The constraints defence is attributed to the revisionist school without a name; Parker is now given his real position.
findings.evidence: Fetched Wikipedia, 'R. A. C. Parker': Chamberlain 'did not pursue appeasement in order to buy time, as some of his defenders claimed'; Parker held an Anglo-French alliance was 'a realistic and more honourable course'. Cross-checked against Lesson 12 content_html.

summary: Every lesson carried at least one exam-format error: a 4-mark 'describe two features' question that does not exist in this section (12 lessons), a 15-mark compare-interpretations question that is worth 25 (7 lessons), and an 8-mark explain question that is worth 10 (6 lessons). Eleven lessons made up claims about what examiners reward, twice quoting invented 'examiner notes' or an internal teaching brief. The substantive history errors are the Warsaw Pact interval (five days, not nine, including a knowledge check whose key was wrong), the lifting of League sanctions on Italy (July 1936, not May), and R.A.C. Parker being credited with the revisionist defence of Chamberlain that he in fact attacked - a misattribution Lesson 12 of the same unit contradicts.
